content: Lortab, also known as hydrocodone/paracetamol or hydrocodone/acetaminophen, is a pharmaceutical combination of two analgesic agents: hydrocodone and paracetamol (acetaminophen). This medication is primarily used to alleviate moderate to severe pain. It is commonly available in tablet form and is marketed under various trade names, including Vicodin, Vicodin ES, Vicodin HP, Anexsia, Anolor DH5, Bancap HC, Zydone, Dolacet, Lorcet, Lortab, and Norco, as well as generic brands. Additionally, hydrocodone is available in combination with ibuprofen under the trade name Vicoprofen. Medical Uses Hydrocodone/paracetamol is an opioid analgesic used for pain management. It is most frequently prescribed for the relief of moderate to moderately severe pain, whether acute, chronic, or post-operative in nature. Formulations This medication is a mixture of hydrocodone and paracetamol. Paracetamol functions as an analgesic and antipyretic, while hydrocodone is a semi-synthetic opioid analgesic. Pregnancy Hydrocodone/paracetamol is classified as a pregnancy category C drug. Insufficient research exists to confirm its safety during pregnancy. However, if taken close to delivery, it may cause respiratory depression in the newborn. Pregnant women who use opioids regularly risk their babies being born substance-dependent, leading to withdrawal symptoms after birth. These symptoms may include excessive crying, vomiting, irritability, tremors, and fever. Nursing mothers are advised against using this drug, as paracetamol is known to transfer through breast milk, though it is unclear whether hydrocodone does. Side Effects Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, dizziness, and lightheadedness. Rare but serious side effects may include allergic reactions, seizures, clammy skin, paranoia, hallucinations, severe weakness, hyperventilation, unconsciousness, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or eyes), unusual fatigue, bleeding, bruising, stomach pain, constipation, dry mouth, decreased appetite, muscle twitches, sweating, hot flashes, itching, tinnitus, hearing loss, decreased urination, and altered libido. Hydrocodone can also depress the central nervous system, potentially causing irritability. Some individuals may seek out the drug for its euphoric and sedative effects, as well as its ability to slow the pulse. Unlike NSAIDs, paracetamol does not cause ulcers but can lead to liver damage if dosages exceed 4000 mg per day. This risk is heightened when using combination drugs like Vicodin. Liver damage can range from abdominal pain to liver failure, potentially requiring a liver transplant to prevent death. It is crucial to adhere to physician-prescribed dosages. Pharmacodynamics The analgesic effects of hydrocodone and paracetamol together exhibit a synergistic interaction that is not fully understood but is believed to involve the inhibition of prostaglandins. Hydrocodone acts on μ-opioid receptors and is metabolized into hydromorphone by the enzyme cytochrome P450 2D6. Another enzyme, cytochrome 3A4, forms norhydrocodone. Hydrocodone crosses the blood-brain barrier, where its analgesic effects are primarily exerted. Many side effects are attributed to its ability to cross this barrier. Paracetamol, on the other hand, inhibits the enzyme cyclooxygenase (COX), which is necessary for prostaglandin production. Prostaglandins mediate pain, fever, and inflammation. Paracetamol’s half-life ranges from 1 to 4 hours, with peak levels occurring 40–60 minutes after ingestion. It is thought to reduce pain by increasing serotonergic neurotransmission. Unlike hydrocodone, paracetamol does not readily cross the blood-brain barrier. Society and Culture Manufacture Hydrocodone, the primary component of Vicodin, shares a similar structure to morphine but is metabolized by different enzymes. Vicodin is available in three variations with differing amounts of hydrocodone. Hydrocodone is approximately twice as potent as morphine when taken orally for acute use. The tablets contain less hydrocodone than paracetamol, as the combination aims to utilize different mechanisms of pain relief while minimizing the adverse effects of each drug by using lower doses. Both hydrocodone and paracetamol are white crystalline powders that are manufactured into tablet form. Manufacturers of hydrocodone include Abbott Laboratories (makers of Vicodin), Amerisource Health Services Corp, Cardinal Health, Drx Pharmaceutical Consultants Inc, Eckerd Corp, Hospira Inc, Mallinckrodt Pharm, Quality Care, Pdrx Pharmaceuticals Inc, Physicians Total Care Inc, Rx Papoo’s Packaging Inc, and Watson Pharmaceuticals. On January 13, 2011, the FDA requested that manufacturers of prescription acetaminophen combination products limit the maximum amount of acetaminophen to 325 mg per tablet, capsule, or dosage unit. This measure aims to reduce the risk of severe liver injury from acetaminophen overdosing, which can lead to liver failure, liver transplant, or death. Legal Status In the United States, Vicodin production is regulated under the Controlled Substances Act of 1970. This law ensures that the manufacturing, importing, possession, and distribution of drugs are overseen by the federal government. Vicodin is classified as a Schedule III drug. Pure hydrocodone and codeine are Schedule II drugs, but when combined with paracetamol or an NSAID, they are classified as Schedule III. Schedule III drugs are considered to have the potential for moderate or low physical dependence or high psychological dependence if misused. To qualify as a Schedule III medication in the United States, hydrocodone must be combined with a non-narcotic ingredient in a recognized therapeutic amount. The FDA advisory panel has recommended removing Vicodin and Percocet from the market due to the high likelihood of overdose from prescription narcotics and acetaminophen products. Concerns about liver damage from the acetaminophen component, which is also found in over-the-counter drugs like Tylenol, were cited. Acetaminophen overdose is linked to approximately 400 deaths and 42,000 hospitalizations annually in the United States. The FDA has given manufacturers three years to limit acetaminophen content in prescription drugs to 325 mg per dosage unit and requires updated labels warning of the risk of severe liver injury. Hydrocodone, the narcotic component of Vicodin, is still available in Canada as a single drug under the trade name Hycodan, marketed in syrup and tablet forms by Bristol-Myers-Squibb. Popular Media The central character of the American television medical drama House habitually uses and abuses Vicodin to manage pain from a quadriceps muscle infarction sustained years earlier. Vicodin is also referenced in multiple songs by rapper Eminem, such as Kill You, Under the Influence, Deja Vu, Old Time's Sake, Underground, Going Through Changes, Oh No, and Cocaine. Eminem featured a Vicodin pill on the CD of his debut album The Slim Shady LP. The rapper has admitted to an addiction to the painkiller, along with other substances, which caused a hiatus in his career and required rehabilitation for his return to music.
